newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed Tuesday, as dealers expected September delivery to trade sideways in a range between 160.00 and 168.00 cents a lb.
Some traders said the market's bias was to the downside, with continued mild temperatures in top-grower Brazil likely to weigh on sentiment.
Weather Services Corp said Tuesday there was no damaging cold weather in sight for Brazil's coffee belt, with temperatures expected to be near to above normal during the next seven days.

Monday, New York arabica futures ended mixed, with benchmark September futures finishing down 2.65 cents at 165.70 cents after trading from 166.50 to 162.10 cents. Spot July ended 2.25 cents lower at 185.25 cents, while the outer months closed up 0.35 to 2.25 cents.
Technically, traders said September faced near-term chart support at 162.00 cents, followed by 158.00 and 155.00 cents. Resistance was seen toward 170.00 cents.
After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 1,926 60-kg bags as of July 4, to 52,476 bags. An additional 35,930 bags were pending exchange approval.

Also after Monday's close, the CFTC Commitments of Traders report for the two weeks ended July 1 showed non-commercial long positions fell by 820 lots, to 3,559 lots. Non-commercial short positions rose by 316 lots, to 1,183 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose by 87 lots to 7,625 lots, while commercial short positions fell by 894 lots to 12,297 lots.
Non-reportable long positions fell by 723 lots to 8,580 lots and nonreportable short positions fell by 908 lots to 6,284 lots.

London robusta futures were mainly firmer by midday on Tuesday after early weakness, buoyed by roaster buying. At the break, benchmark September stood $13 higher at $1,790, after ranging from $1,795 to $1,762.
